newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page - Mar 10.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page - Mar 10.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following stories on its front page on Monday:
* The U.S. Congress has begun debating the role of government in regulating health care and seems likely to set standards for health maintenance organizations.
* The scandal over Democratic fund-raising methods involving Chinese businesses and contacts is complicating U.S. policy toward China as leaders from both countries prepare to meet.

* The latest Nielsen ratings show more than one million fewer homes watched television in February compared to a year earlier, marking the fourth year out of five in which overall prime-time viewing has declined. Television industry executives challenge such figures and have united to support an experimental rival to the Nielsen's rating system.

* Americans are relinquishing their right to sue in the wake of corporate notices detailing new arbitration requirements and recent court decisions making it easier for companies to demand that claims be handled out of court.

* As Islam grows increasingly popular in the Netherlands, Catholic and Protestant churchs there are confronting the same question faced by their American counterparts: What to do with the many chapels and monasteries that are now unused.

* A Latino and Hispanic section of Brooklyn, New York, where nearly half of the residents receive public assistance, is already showing the effects of welfare legislation putting more restrictions on government aid.
* A group of old friends and former felons have organized themselves as the Alliance of Concerned Men of Washington D.C., a group seeking to fight crime and reduce youth violence across the country.
